thread:
oncall-bot: Pager: high p95 latency on runtime-serving in us-west after canary deploy (service=runtime, env=prod). Threshold breached: p95 > 400ms for 3m.
oncall-bot: Incident auto-created: INC-20260315-1842500000 — paging oncall.
Sam W: I'm on it. seeing a jump in tail latency and a throughput dip on the canary pool.
Ivy C: Confirming. dashboards show kernel-fallback events spiking for 3 hosts in canary set (host-23/24/25). KV cache hit rate drops too.
Jordan P: @Sam W @Ivy C any recent change? which commit/deploy touched runtime batching or kernel selection?
Emily R: Canary was traffic-shift 10% -> 30% 09:01 UTC. Released runtime v2.14.3 with new kernel-affinity heuristics and a batching tweak (continuous batching aggressiveness +0.2).
Sam W: ok. hypothesis: new kernel-affinity + batching change is causing fallback to slower path under this workload.
Leo H: Logs:
```
[host-23] 09:04:12 WARN kernel_fallback: selected kernel unsupported for quantized path, falling back to generic_cpu.
[host-23] 09:04:12 WARN batching: batch size mismatch, falling back to single-request path
```
Sam W: Those kernel_fallback messages match the p95 spike.
deploy-bot: Canary traffic currently at 30%. To rollback: `/deploy rollback --release v2.14.3 --target canary`
Ivy C: Trying quick mitigation — can we toggle the canary kernel-affinity flag back? feature flag name: runtime.kernel_affinity.v2
Sam W: yes. patching flag now.
Sam W: `curl -s -X POST https://controlplane.internal/flags/runtime.kernel_affinity.v2 -d '{"value": false}'`
oncall-bot: Flag update acknowledged (actor=Sam W).
Ivy C: Re-running canary health checks. kernel-fallback logs dropping on host-23. p95 trending down.
Jordan P: Oncall: please hold ramp to 40% while we validate. Also -- disable batching aggressiveness tweak remotely? can we flip runtime.batching.aggr.v2 -> 0.0
Emily R: Pushing batching flag to 0.0 now. `PATCH /flags/runtime.batching.aggr.v2`
ops-bot: Flag runtime.batching.aggr.v2 updated by Emily R.
Sam W: Good, p95 back to baseline on canary pool (p95 ~ 120ms). throughput normalizing.
Ivy C: But we still see a handful of requests hitting generic_cpu kernels on host-24 intermittently. investigating kernel version skew and supported kernel matrix.
Jordan P: Given instability, recommend rolling back the canary release and aborting the full rollout. Any customer impact?
Sam W: Quick check: error-rate not elevated, requests mostly just slower. Customer-facing: a subset of low-latency customers (tenant IDs: tenant-98, tenant-342) reported higher response times in the last 10m via alerts.
Emily R: Noting: no 5xxs. No data exfiltration. No config changes that touch auth. This looks performance-only.
Sam W: Initiating rollback of v2.14.3 canary.
deploy-bot: Rollback command received. Starting rollback to v2.14.2 on canary hosts. Progress: host-23 OK, host-24 OK, host-25 OK. All canary hosts reverted.
Ivy C: After rollback, kernel_fallback logs cease. p95 stable at baseline across canary and stable pools.
Jordan P: Great. Please flip kill-switch on the new kernel-selection rollout to prevent accidental re-rollouts while we investigate. Flag: rollout.runtime.kernel_affinity.v2 -> disabled
Sam W: Kill-switch set. `POST /control/rollouts/disable?name=kernel_affinity_v2` -> 200 OK.
oncall-bot: Incident update: rollback completed, kill-switch engaged, canary traffic frozen.
Ivy C: Customer impact assessment: tenant-98 and tenant-342 saw median latency bump ~+250ms for ~8-12 minutes during the spike. No errors reported. We'll reach out proactively with details.
Emily R: Mitigation summary: 1) toggled kernel_affinity flag off 2) reset batching aggressiveness 3) rolled back release on canary 4) engaged kill-switch.
Sam W: Postmortem actions: - Run integration test that simulates our prefix/KV cache distribution vs kernel selection to catch fallback cases. - Add an automated canary probe that stresses batching edge-cases. - Validate kernel compatibility matrix in CI.
Jordan P: I'll open PM-INC ticket and assign leads (Ivy/Emily) for root cause. Also sync with model-onboarding team — maybe compilers produced unsupported kernels for quantized models.
ops-bot: Created ticket PM-INC-789 (owner=Jordan P, priority=P1, due=2026-03-18).
Sam W: Final check: monitoring for 30m. I'll handoff to Ivy for post-incident follow-ups.
Ivy C: Taking handoff. I'll update affected customers and schedule RCA. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
oncall-bot: Incident status -> mitigated. Will auto-close after 24h if no regressions observed.
